subtype: Approach: noticing warning signs and taking them seriously [Thinking]
passage:
'You've been rubbing your eyes since nine,' said Tejas, sliding into the seat across from Vaibhav in the canteen. 'And you snapped at the intern over a typo.'
'I know.' Vaibhav stirred the tea without drinking it. 'I've been tired every day for weeks, even after a Sunday lie-in. And last night around eight I got that dread in my stomach about Monday. Third Sunday running.'
'Maybe you just need a rest weekend.'
'I thought that too. But I've had rest weekends. The tiredness is back by Tuesday. That's not one bad week. It's a pattern.'
'So?'
'So I'm not going to push through it. Something in how I work has to change. I'll talk to my manager about the team's load, and I'll see a doctor if it doesn't lift.'
Tejas nodded slowly. 'Good. I'll take the Thursday review off your list.'

qa.q: What did Vaibhav say happens after a rest weekend?
qa.a: Vaibhav said the tiredness is back by Tuesday.

qa.q: What was Vaibhav feeling on Sunday nights?
qa.a: Vaibhav felt a stomach-tightening dread about Monday.

qa.q: What other approach could Vaibhav take besides resting?
qa.a: Vaibhav could change how the work is shared by talking to the manager, hand off tasks, and see a doctor if the tiredness does not lift.

qa.q: How might Tejas see Vaibhav's situation?
qa.a: Tejas seems concerned and supportive, noticing the signs and offering to take the Thursday review.

grounding: Vaibhav notices constant tiredness, irritability and Sunday-night dread and treats them as a pattern that needs change, not just a rest weekend.
